summary.name: Unitree AlienGo
summary.one_liner: AlienGo is a 12-motor quadruped (robot dog) from Unitree Robotics, with depth and visual-odometry cameras, aimed at research and industrial use.
use_cases: attaching cameras, lidar or robotic arms
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a quadruped robot with 12 high-performance servo motors that can run, jump, climb slopes and steps, and recover from a fall. Its maximum walking speed is stated as over 1.5 m/s, with a rated load of 13 kg and a weight of 21.5 kg without battery. Sensing includes two depth cameras (minimum depth 0.11 m, up to 1280x720) and one visual odometry camera for V-SLAM, with optional single or multi-line lidar. The control software exposes high-level and low-level interfaces supporting C/C++ and ROS, and the developer version includes an onboard PC plus Ethernet, USB and 485 ports for user add-on modules. Battery endurance is listed as 2.5 to 4.6 hours.
notable: 12 servo motors with full 3-axis attitude and position control
Two depth cameras plus a visual odometry camera for V-SLAM
Open software interface with C/C++ and ROS support, and per-motor or per-leg control
Developer version includes an onboard PC and expansion interfaces
caveats: Page describes the robot as a civilian product; dangerous modifications or hazardous use are discouraged
Specifications may change without notice; the actual product prevails
Lidar is optional rather than included
Price is not listed on the page
